# CS-010: Public SSH has brute force protection on the right port

- **Group:** CrowdSec and fail2ban
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

SSH open to anywhere draws constant password guessing. A fail2ban sshd jail or the CrowdSec sshd collection bans repeat offenders. A jail watching port 22 while sshd listens elsewhere bans on the wrong port and protects nothing.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo fail2ban-client status sshd; sudo cscli collections list | grep sshd; ss -tlnp | grep sshd
```

## How to fix it

Enable an sshd jail with port set to the real sshd port, or install the crowdsecurity/sshd collection

Run `stackward explain CS-010` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
